cards.headline: Low-Rise Ordinance adopted
cards.summary: LAMC residential zoning amendments take effect alongside SB 79 on July 1, 2026. Adds 17,562 sites that retain ≥ 50% SB 79 capacity under local rules — meaning SB 79 will apply to ~29,000 fewer sites than the un-amended baseline.

cards.headline: CPC recommends approval of LA's two SB 79 ordinances
cards.summary: City Planning Commission voted to recommend approval of the Low-Rise Ordinance (CPC-2026-1797-CA) and Phased Implementation Ordinance (CPC-2026-1798-MSC), advancing LA's strategy to delay full SB 79 effectuation until 2030 via temporary exemptions.

cards.headline: Why does LA oppose SB 79?
cards.summary: Industry analysis of LA's resistance contrasted with Culver City's 4,500-unit SB 79 pipeline. Developer-side reaction described as cautious due to LA's implementation uncertainty.

cards.headline: Draft SB 79 ordinances released for public review
cards.summary: City Planning published drafts of the Phased Implementation Ordinance and Low-Rise Ordinance covering 55 station areas, opening the public comment period.

cards.headline: Cities scramble as SB 79 deadline nears
cards.summary: CalMatters investigates how LA, SF, Oakland and Sacramento are responding to SB 79's July 1 effective date. Highlights LA's maximum-delay strategy through the Low-Rise Ordinance + Phased Implementation Model.

cards.headline: City Council adopts Option C1 — phased SB 79 compliance by 2030
cards.summary: Council directed Planning to pursue phased implementation while expanding the Corridor Transition program, excluding HPOZs from upzoning.

cards.headline: PLUM Committee findings published
cards.summary: Planning and Land Use Management Committee held hearing on SB 79 implementation framework. Findings support the Phased Implementation Model methodology and identify open coordination items with HCD on industrial-zoned land treatment.

cards.headline: LA Metro Board seeks SB 79 exemption
cards.summary: 11 of 13 Metro board members voted to support LA County exemption from SB 79, citing concerns about transit expansion opposition. SB 677 introduced to provide technical fixes.

cards.headline: Courts reaffirm state housing laws preempt charter cities
cards.summary: Rancho Palos Verdes v. State and Kennedy Commission decisions establish that charter cities have minimal home-rule defense against SB 79. Strengthens enforceability against LA's anticipated charter-city objections.

cards.headline: Critical finding: SB 79 height limits are hard caps
cards.summary: Holland & Knight analysis reveals local agencies are NOT required to grant Density Bonus Law waivers/concessions beyond SB 79's stated height floors, even though they must grant them for density and FAR. This breaks the typical SDBL stacking assumption — projects cannot exceed 95 ft (Tier 1) or 85 ft (Tier 2) regardless of bonus units.

cards.headline: Newsom signs SB 79 — landmark transit housing law
cards.summary: Governor signs the Abundant and Affordable Homes Near Transit Act. Statewide effective date July 1, 2026. HAA presumptive-violation enforcement begins January 1, 2027 — six-month soft launch window.
